integrity: The feasibility wedge is obtained by exact sign analysis and factorization of the printed two-sided k-bound. All baseline interval endpoints are reproduced with exact rational arithmetic by the bundled checker. The source's stated baseline values and Assumption 4 were inspected directly.
scientific_limitations: The result is a domain-of-validity theorem for the printed Assumption-4 inequalities; it does not solve the constrained Stackelberg game outside that domain.
Numerical trajectories outside Assumption 4 are not declared false; their interpretation requires a separate constrained-optimization justification.
The third feasibility condition involving sustainable-fulfillment effort and cost is not needed for the exclusion and may further shrink the admissible set.
title: An exact feasibility wedge excludes the low-emission baseline in a green supply-chain game
